summary: A tight two-player Knizia classic where each turn you either advance one of your color-coded expeditions or discard, weighing the risk of committing early against a colored suit's steep negative starting cost. It plays fast and rewards careful hand-reading and push-your-luck judgment about how many suits to invest in.
praised: elegant, minimal rules hiding real decision depth
quick, tense push-your-luck play perfect for two players
great as a filler or a 'one more round' game
cards and components hold up well over many plays
criticised: can feel mathematical or dry to players who dislike Knizia's abstract style
meaningful luck in what you draw versus what's available
limited long-term variability since there's no variable setup

interaction.detail: Each player builds their own separate expeditions in front of them, but the shared discard piles mean you're constantly deciding whether to hand your opponent a useful card or deny them one. It's mostly parallel play punctuated by these discard-timing decisions.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Every point comes from the same mechanism — an expedition's played-card total minus its entry cost, multiplied by any handshake cards — just applied separately to each of the color suits.
scoring.how_you_win: Play cards to build ascending expeditions in the colors worth pursuing (each costs 20 points to open), discard the rest, then sum all expedition scores across three hands; the higher total wins.
